issue.title: [Canonical #22; completed] Unified DOC game and automatic CPU/WebGPU validation
issue.body:
Public development tracking for the original [DOC #22](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/22). The canonical issue numbers and acceptance decision stay in imxade/DOC. This issue does not imply a completed migration of GitHub issue history.

# Blocking prerequisite to DOC→C Issue #11: unified game proof + native automatic heterogeneous scheduling

Requested 2026-11-24. **Do not begin Issue #11 until both acceptance families below have demonstrated, exact-source validation.** Scoped #10 remains closed for its earlier agreed acceptance; this is a new, stronger integration/architecture gate. GUI/editor, automatic art assets, and 3D remain deferred as #21.

## A. One small DOC-authored game demonstrates most implemented features

- [x] Add one runnable, minimal, repeatable game on the existing DOC language/engine, **not** a host-Rust imitation or collection of unrelated demonstrations.
- [x] Cover most applicable 2D/headless capabilities in a coherent playthrough: typed data-driven level/prefab entities, spawn/despawn/handles, collision/query, deterministic fixed-step input and timers/animation, score/win, save/load+restore, replay, explicit audio-file effect, typed assets and safe failure path. Clearly identify any feature verified only in ancillary tests.
- [x] Provide a single documented command or script to run the combined demo; add end-to-end black-box tests, oracle/replay parity, negative and resource cases. Optional WebGPU *presentation* has a separate hardware provenance.
- [x] Run the real combined game, not just check that it compiles, on 1/2/4/8 workers.

## B. Automatic native scheduling from DOC independence

- [x] Gameplay DOC contains *no* CPU-worker, GPU, placement, partition or device instructions: dependencies determine independence; runtime/engine chooses scheduling automatically.
- [x] Prove true parallel CPU evaluation of ready independent DOC nodes and transparent scheduling on small/single-core systems. A CPU thread count parameter is test/evidence control only, not source scheduling.
- [x] Implement safe, bounded **automatic CPU/GPU partition where hardware is available** for eligible independent ready tasks; CPU independently handles non-GPU-compatible tasks from the *same* DOC graph/epoch. Explicit selected-CPU/GPU modes remain strict separate interfaces; no CPU work may be reported as actual GPU dispatch.
- [x] Do not hide host-side gameplay rules, prelabel every game node manually, or claim shader presentation as GPU *compute*. Determine eligibility from typed DOC expressions. Preserve original ordering/dependency semantics, lazy errors and complete publication on any failure. Detect adapter/limits; no-device or unsupported work must honestly execute on CPU in auto mode (and be reported as such).
- [x] Report scheduler decision & actual workload breakdown with physical-GPU vs software-adapter labels. Test a **genuine mixed independent frontier** with a GPU-eligible work partition and CPU-only partition from the same real game. On Mesa, label it software-only; hardware-only claims require physical adapter proof.
- [x] Differential tests (auto vs CPU oracle) across deterministic replay, changes, invalid inputs, missing GPU, injected GPU/CPU failure, and 1/2/4/8 workers. Explicitly validate that failed epochs do not partially publish.
- [x] Measure overhead, latency and resource lifecycle; avoid gratuitous GPU context creation per tiny tick. State any bounded/gating policy and limits honestly.

## Exit/contract

- [x] Current SHA passes both Linux Rust/CPU and software-WebGPU CI including combined game, real dispatch provenance and negative tests. Physical GPU proof is separately labeled and not fabricated.
- [x] Update engine documentation, capability matrix and issue ledger; record commands, concrete outputs, limitations and exact source SHA.
- [x] Only then close this issue and explicitly confirm readiness for #11. If incomplete, leave OPEN and keep #11 on hold.

Reference: #10 accepted a smaller set of separately validated slices. This issue intentionally adds the missing **single coherent demo** and **automatic CPU/GPU workload distribution** requirement. Future DOC→C work is #11; do not substitute codegen or a new language to implement this gate.

## Public migration
The source snapshot import [f3327d8](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/commit/f3327d8ff61d84316282884731022b8cc6dedd98) has all 596 paths, modes, and Git blob hashes of the private working tree at 142c47958a80df0345bd6c26ec8ad31d9e085a90. Main is the active branch. Validate the public revision, not the old private Actions runs. No credentials copied. Optional physical Kaggle runs are explicitly gated; the Linux CPU/software-WebGPU gate remains mandatory.

## Final acceptance — 2026-11-24 — COMPLETE

Exact sole public main revision: [0f186a8a1b5d71023f6d19100d1ed4ad16a49c5b](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/commit/0f186a8a1b5d71023f6d19100d1ed4ad16a49c5b). Both mandatory [native Linux CPU and software-WebGPU jobs](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45323487472) passed; [physical Kaggle Tesla T4 job](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45323904580) also passed on this exact SHA and verified native bundle from 45323487472. [Physical raw evidence artifact](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45323904580/artifacts/14889280764), bundle SHA256 1bf3af2e353eba6aa2cbf25df97eb5f47abfe976ac963ea65e0aaa55f860b5e1; downloaded archive of logs SHA256 34501cc0afc499bc404d3c594b3c1f1f274860dbc8bbdcd54b57ed77c29ea3c5.

- Unified DOC-authored Radar Chase runs on the existing Rust engine, without placement or worker hints in game source. Real winning replay `edsssxwddddsspr` ends at tick 13, (6,4), score 2, then pauses and restarts. 1/2/4/8 requested workers and automatic default agree; actual CPU parallelism capped by available logical processors, one-worker serial control, four-worker execution of 142-state ready frontiers. 145 native Rust tests and 34 WebGPU-job test executions passed (some overlap), with black-box replay, native packaging, capacity/stale identities, typed reload rejection, checkpoint/restore and actual WAV output, animation, safe failure/atomic publication, strict explicit backend behavior, natural no-device fallback. Ancillary resource/lifetime/graph tests supplement the game.
- CPU only: 2,940 derived evaluations, 15 parallel and 150 CPU-only frontiers in the 15-tick replay. Automatic physical and software WebGPU each: 930 CPU + 2,010 GPU evaluations, 15 mixed frontiers of 8 CPU and 134 GPU states, 15 actual GPU dispatches of three 64-lane workgroups; one created session and 14 reuses. No GPU source directives. Verified physical selection Tesla T4 / DiscreteGpu (vendor 4318, device 7864); no software marker; software CI independently labeled software-test-only. Downloaded physical logs independently compared all 48 frame/entity/radar records exactly against CPU, 16 frames including epoch zero. Injected stage-zero GPU failure retains only initial frame, no successor publication. Device/session reuse verified. Physical suite also passed 42 native signed GPU episodes and 62 selected DOC source cases, plus 27 benchmark samples.
- Comparable same-host physical run, 15 steps (recurrence advance only; includes first GPU initialization): CPU p50/p95 1842/2732 µs, peak RSS 4500 KiB; mixed physical p50/p95 5341/307789 µs, peak RSS 323920 KiB. Separate GitHub five-step samples: CPU 1148/1195 µs RSS 3632 KiB; software mixed 1934/31623 µs RSS 91676 KiB. GPU scheduling correctness and resource reuse proven, NOT speedup: tiny workloads can be slower, initialization and transfers matter. Current >=64 eligible scalar lanes is a bounded admission policy, not a universal profitability predictor; noneligible expressions remain CPU. Initial epoch and restore admission use CPU. GUI/editor, generated assets, general ECS/3D/live audio/physical presentation are outside scoped #22 (deferred #21). See [game documentation](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/blob/0f186a8a1b5d71023f6d19100d1ed4ad16a49c5b/engine/RADAR-CHASE.md) and [capability matrix](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/blob/0f186a8a1b5d71023f6d19100d1ed4ad16a49c5b/engine/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md), updated in the validated main ancestry.
- Reproduction from repository root: `cargo run --release --manifest-path runtime-rust/Cargo.toml --features webgpu --bin doc-game -- engine/radar_chase.doc --headless --measure --replay=edsssxwddddsspr`. Omit --features webgpu for CPU-only build. Explicit software admission is test-only. CPU oracle override DOC_AUTO_DISABLE_GPU=1 is a test/evidence control, never game source placement.
- [Single branch cleanup](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45323278639) passed; only main remains, historical branch snapshots retained as ancestors, old private repository untouched. Temporary write-enabled cleanup workflow removed. No further source commit needed to preserve exact final tested SHA.

All scoped #22 gates are satisfied. Public #1 and canonical #22 can close completed. Canonical #11 / public #2 is now READY for the DOC → generated C → native executable milestone; no implementation of #11 is claimed or begun. #10 remains closed and #21 remains deferred.

## Public CI checkpoint (not final acceptance)
The exact public main SHA 34f22a512d74f9828807148517112bae83f14168 is now running successfully on GitHub-hosted runners. [Native CPU job](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45320305608/job/138196971216) completed success: 144 reported passing Rust test cases in 51 suites (no failures). Actual game worker 1/2/4/8 plus default output parity passed. Default automatic replay on 4 logical CPUs evaluated 2940 DOC states over 15 epochs, with 15 parallel frontiers and 150 CPU-only frontiers; one worker reported zero parallel frontiers. Five-step CPU-only game measurement p50 1165 us, p95 1290 us, peak process RSS 3620 KiB; this is a small hosted-runner sample, not a general speed claim. Linux installed executable smoke passed. The software-WebGPU job is still executing. The public repo is no longer exhibiting the private runner allocation failure. Keep both tracking issues open pending actual mixed compute and exact-SHA 2/2.

## First public exact-source CI: both jobs pass
[Run 45320305608](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45320305608), main SHA 34f22a512d74f9828807148517112bae83f14168: CPU and software-WebGPU jobs both completed success. Native GPU logs showed five independent mixed frontiers each 8 CPU + 134 GPU states, actual WGSL dispatch 3 groups of 64 lanes, totals 310 CPU / 670 GPU nodes over five steps, a single GPU session and pipeline with reuse, and injected GPU error before successor publication. Software adapter only. Five-tick sample CPU p50 1165 µs / p95 1290 µs / RSS 3620 KiB; mixed software-WebGPU p50 1029 µs / p95 20575 µs / RSS 92128 KiB (includes initialization, tiny runner sample, not a general speedup claim).

The active strengthening candidate 770e64692e5753c02eecd92746d9eed364d34f4b on feat/webgpu-dual-runtime-ci adds a complete mixed winning replay, no-admitted-device CPU fallback without force flags, mixed-feature binary replay/save/audio checks, capacity/stale-ID and animation assertions.
